newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes rebound, short coverings sink grades.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes rebound, short coverings sink grades.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes rebounded Friday afternoon on short coverings, while sweet grade differentials sank on a short squeeze in the February/March West Texas Intermediate roll, traders said.

The Feb/March spread moved out to around $1.08 a barrel, up from 81-83 cents this morning. The sharp upturn drove deals for WTI/Cushing Posting Plus as high as $2.79 a barrel, up about 30 cents from late Thursday.
February WTI/Cushing was trading around $25.70-80 a barrel, up 30 cents from late Thursday's cash market. WTI had dropped this morning in line with lower heating oil prices.
Sweet grades plunged as traders moved into more lucrative territory. "With high values on Posting Plus, people want to get out of the grades and capture value there," a Texas broker said.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St.James got done at 20 cents a barrel below WTI/Cushing, down from an eight cent discount earlier in the day, traders said.
WTI/Midland fared better, changing hands at WTI/Cushing minus 33 cents, steady with late Thursday.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was slightly weaker at WTI/Cushing minus 50 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland was done at a $1.70 discount to WTI/Cushing, down four cents from the lowest priced deal on Thursday.
